Clean Architecture Transition Plan

A comprehensive roadmap for transforming the Anplexa platform from a monolithic structure to a layered Clean Architecture, improving testability, maintainability, and scalability.

35%

Transition Overview

Why Clean Architecture and what it means for Anplexa

⚠

Current Problems

  • Fat Controllers: authRoutes.ts has 985 lines mixing HTTP, business logic, and data access
  • No Domain Layer: Business rules scattered across route handlers
  • Untestable: Cannot unit test business logic in isolation
  • Tight Coupling: Components directly depend on external frameworks
  • God Components: ChatInterface.tsx is 949 lines with 12+ useEffect hooks
✓

Target Benefits

  • Testability: Use cases can be unit tested with mocks
  • Maintainability: Clear separation of concerns
  • Flexibility: Swap frameworks without changing business logic
  • Scalability: Team can work on different layers independently
  • Readability: Smaller, focused components and functions
🛠

Apps Affected

Backend API (2-terminal-companion)
Express.js + TypeScript + Drizzle ORM


Companions App (v0-ai-companion-prototype)
Next.js 16 + React 19 + AI SDK v5


Marketing Funnel (Funnel-Forge)
Vite + React 19 + Express.js

📋

Key Principles

The Dependency Rule:

Source code dependencies can only point inward. Inner layers know nothing about outer layers.


Entities Over Frameworks:

Business entities should not depend on frameworks. A User entity shouldn't know about Express or React.

The Dependency Rule

Dependencies point inward. Outer layers depend on inner layers, never the reverse.

Presentation (HTTP)
→
Infrastructure (DB)
→
Application (Use Cases)
→
Domain (Entities)

Domain layer has ZERO external dependencies. It defines interfaces that outer layers implement.

📁

Architecture Layers

The four concentric layers of Clean Architecture

Presentation Layer
HTTP routes, controllers, React components, validators
↓
Infrastructure Layer
Database implementations, external APIs, frameworks
↓
Application Layer
Use cases, DTOs, application services
↓
Domain Layer (Core)
Entities, value objects, repository interfaces, domain services
Domain

Domain Layer

Purpose: Enterprise business rules that would exist even without software.


Contains:

  • Entities (User, Conversation, Message)
  • Value Objects (Email, Password, Token)
  • Repository Interfaces (IUserRepository)
  • Domain Services (CreditService)
  • Domain Errors (AuthenticationError)

Zero external dependencies!

Application

Application Layer

Purpose: Application-specific business rules. Orchestrates data flow between layers.


Contains:

  • Use Cases (LoginUser, SendMessage)
  • DTOs (LoginRequest, LoginResponse)
  • Application Services (TokenService)
  • Port Interfaces (IEmailService)

Depends only on Domain layer.

Infrastructure

Infrastructure Layer

Purpose: Implements interfaces defined by inner layers. Contains all framework details.


Contains:

  • Repository Implementations (DrizzleUserRepository)
  • External Service Adapters (OllamaGateway)
  • Database Configuration
  • Email Service (SendGrid)

Implements domain interfaces.

Presentation

Presentation Layer

Purpose: Converts external requests to use case inputs and formats outputs.


Contains:

  • HTTP Routes (thin, < 100 lines)
  • Controllers (request/response handling)
  • Validators (Zod schemas)
  • Middleware (auth, rate limiting)

Calls use cases, handles HTTP concerns only.

🖥

Backend Migration

Transforming the Express.js API to Clean Architecture

Current vs Target Structure

Before

Current Structure

server/ presentation/routes/ authRoutes.ts # 985 lines! chatRoutes.ts # 640 lines! stripeRoutes.ts # 472 lines infrastructure/ adapters/ database/ shared/ schema.ts # ORM only
After

Target Structure

server/ domain/ entities/ # User, Conversation value-objects/ # Email, Token repositories/ # Interfaces only application/ use-cases/ # LoginUser, SendMessage dto/ # Request/Response shapes infrastructure/ persistence/ # Repository impls external/ # Ollama, Stripe presentation/ routes/ # < 100 lines each! controllers/

Example: LoginUser Use Case Extraction

// domain/entities/User.ts
export class User {
  constructor(
    public readonly id: string,
    public readonly email: Email,
    private readonly passwordHash: string
  ) {}

  async validatePassword(password: string): Promise<boolean> {
    return bcrypt.compare(password, this.passwordHash);
  }
}

// application/use-cases/auth/LoginUser.ts
export class LoginUser {
  constructor(
    private readonly userRepo: IUserRepository,
    private readonly tokenService: TokenService
  ) {}

  async execute(request: LoginRequest): Promise<LoginResponse> {
    const user = await this.userRepo.findByEmail(request.email);
    if (!user) throw new AuthenticationError('Invalid credentials');

    const valid = await user.validatePassword(request.password);
    if (!valid) throw new AuthenticationError('Invalid credentials');

    return {
      accessToken: this.tokenService.generateAccessToken(user),
      refreshToken: this.tokenService.generateRefreshToken(user),
      user: { id: user.id, email: user.email.value }
    };
  }
}

// presentation/routes/authRoutes.ts (now < 100 lines)
router.post('/login',
  validateRequest(loginSchema),
  async (req, res, next) => {
    try {
      const result = await loginUser.execute(req.body);
      res.json(result);
    } catch (error) {
      next(error);
    }
  }
);

Frontend Migration

Decomposing React components and extracting hooks

ChatInterface Decomposition

Before

God Component

949 lines

  • 12+ useEffect hooks
  • Message rendering logic
  • Input handling
  • Conversation management
  • Guest mode logic
  • Settings modal
  • Theme handling
  • Scroll management
  • Error handling
After

Decomposed

< 200 lines

  • ChatInterface.tsx - Orchestrator only
  • MessageList.tsx - Render messages
  • MessageItem.tsx - Single message
  • MessageInput.tsx - Input with send
  • useChat.ts - Chat state hook
  • useConversation.ts - CRUD hook
  • useGuestMode.ts - Guest logic hook

Target Component Structure

components/ chat/ ChatInterface.tsx # < 200 lines, orchestration MessageList.tsx # Message rendering MessageItem.tsx # Single message MessageInput.tsx # Input component TypingIndicator.tsx ConversationHeader.tsx hooks/ useChat.ts # Chat state & operations useConversation.ts # Conversation CRUD useGuestMode.ts # Guest mode logic useScrollToBottom.ts services/ api/ client.ts # Axios/fetch config auth.ts # Auth API calls chat.ts # Chat API calls storage/ conversations.ts # localStorage

Auth Context Refactor

Problem: Current auth-context.tsx (~300 lines) mixes:

  • State management
  • Direct API calls (fetch)
  • Token storage (localStorage)
  • Loading/error states

Solution: Adapter pattern

  • AuthService - API calls only
  • TokenStorage - Storage abstraction
  • AuthContext - State only (< 150 lines)
📅

Implementation Phases

Step-by-step migration plan

Phase 1

Foundation Setup

Create directory structure, base classes, and dependency injection.

  • Create domain/, application/, infrastructure/, presentation/ directories
  • Set up base Error classes (DomainError, ValidationError, AuthenticationError)
  • Configure tsyringe or similar DI container
  • Create repository interfaces (IUserRepository, IConversationRepository)
  • Set up barrel exports (index.ts files)
Phase 2

Auth Domain Extraction

Extract authentication logic into use cases.

  • Create User entity with validatePassword method
  • Create Email and Password value objects
  • Extract LoginUser use case from authRoutes.ts
  • Extract RegisterUser use case
  • Extract RefreshToken use case
  • Implement UserRepository with Drizzle
  • Create AuthController (thin controller)
  • Add unit tests for use cases
Phase 3

Chat Domain Extraction

Extract chat and conversation logic.

  • Create Conversation and Message entities
  • Extract SendMessage use case with streaming
  • Extract GetConversationHistory use case
  • Create IAIProvider interface for Ollama
  • Implement ConversationRepository
  • Create ChatController
  • Add integration tests for chat flow
Phase 4

Frontend Refactor

Decompose components and extract hooks.

  • Extract useChat hook from ChatInterface
  • Extract useConversation hook
  • Extract useGuestMode hook
  • Create MessageList and MessageItem components
  • Create MessageInput component
  • Refactor ChatInterface to use new hooks/components
  • Create service layer (authService, chatService)
  • Refactor AuthContext to use adapters
  • Add error boundaries
  • Add unit tests for hooks
📈
